title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt
abstract: arXiv:2611.29824v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent benchmarks are usually made harder by scaling up the data their tasks are built from, yet models that do well on them still fail at real work. We propose building simulated tasks from a model's own attempt at an open-ended task in the real world, so that the model's failures in the simulation resemble its failures in reality. As a case study, we had GPT-6.1 Sol manage two human workers in Cairo over chat for five shifts, with a budget of 7,000 Egyptian pounds, to build as many USB desk lamps as it could. It built two. From the real-world attempt's transcript, we build Memphis, an evaluation in a model-simulated world. Memphis is hard: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers 1.0 lamp per trial on average and repeats its real-world mistakes, buying too few stands and giving up the search for them. With a one-page hint on where to buy parts and who can wire them, it delivers 9.2. Claude Opus 5.5 delivers 2.2 without the hint and 4.6 with it. We release

translated_title: Memphis：从模型真实世界尝试中播种智能体任务的案例研究
translated_abstract: 智能体基准测试通常通过扩大任务所基于的数据规模来增加难度，然而在这些测试上表现良好的模型在真实工作中仍然会失败。我们提出从模型自身在现实世界中对开放性任务的尝试出发来构建模拟任务，使模型在模拟中的失败能够反映其在现实中的失败。作为案例研究，我们让GPT-6.1 Sol通过聊天在开罗管理两名人类工人，进行五个班次，预算为7,000埃及镑，目标是制造尽可能多的USB台灯。它只制造了两盏。从这次真实世界尝试的对话记录中，我们构建了Memphis，一个基于模型模拟世界的评估任务。Memphis难度很高：GPT-6.1 Sol平均每次尝试仅交付1.0盏台灯，并重复了它在现实世界中的错误——购买的灯架太少并放弃了寻找灯架。在获得一页关于在哪里购买零件以及谁能接线提示的情况下，它交付了9.2盏。Claude Opus 5.5在没有提示时交付2.2盏，有提示时交付4.6盏。我们发布了……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 本文提出一种构建智能体评估任务的新方法——从模型自身在现实世界完成开放性任务的记录（如GPT-6.1 Sol在开罗用7000埃及镑造USB台灯仅成功两盏）中播种出模拟任务Memphis，使模型在模拟环境中的失败能真实复现其现实世界的失败，从而生成更能反映真实能力的基准测试。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Memphis, an agent benchmark seeded from GPT-6.1 Sol's real-world attempt to build USB desk lamps in Cairo, showing that simulated tasks derived from a model's own real-world failures reproduce those failures, yielding evaluations that better reflect real-world performance.
